why:
MERGED 2026-09-07 during the phase-428 W10 rebase onto main, from two independent rows that both landed -- main's and this branch's. Both reached the same verdict; the prose is combined here and neither is lost.

the REP-2002 transition set as a closed `enum class LifecycleTransition : uint8_t` (`rclcpp_lifecycle/lifecycle_node.hpp:65`). rclcpp has no such type: it takes a raw `uint8_t` and a porting user reaches for `lifecycle_msgs::msg::Transition::TRANSITION_*`, which is an INTERFACE PACKAGE constant, not a rclcpp type -- so within this lane there is nothing to correspond to. The Rust half is `rust:LifecycleTransition`, ledgered `extension` for the same reason, and this row is half of what `cpp:Transition` records as OUR LANGUAGES DISAGREE: C++ now has the id enum. It is NOT rclcpp's `Transition` class, which also carries `start_state` / `goal_state` / `label`; that one is still the gap `cpp:Transition` describes.

The ids ARE upstream's, and were not always: issue 1099 found ours crossed four of eight values (ours had `Activate = 2` where upstream has `CLEANUP = 2`), so a ported file calling `trigger_transition(TRANSITION_CLEANUP)` on an Inactive node was silently ACTIVATING it and returning ok. `ErrorRecovery = 60` is upstream's implicit error-recovery success edge; upstream `8` is `TRANSITION_DESTROY`, which nano-ros does not implement and `trigger_transition` rejects.

`enum class nros::LifecycleTransition : uint8_t` -- the REP-2002 transition set as a closed enum, added by issue 1099 (PR #602), and ours-only by construction: rclcpp has no transition ENUM. Its callers write `lifecycle_msgs::msg::Transition::TRANSITION_*` constants against `trigger_transition(uint8_t)`, or hold a `lifecycle_msgs::msg::Transition` OBJECT (see `cpp:Transition`, which stays a gap -- the object carries `label`/`start_state`/`goal_state`, and an enum is not that). The discriminants ARE those constants -- `Configure = 1`, `Cleanup = 2`, `Activate = 3`, `Deactivate = 4`, the three shutdowns `5`/`6`/`7` -- so a ported file's raw byte and our enum name the same transition; `ErrorRecovery = 60` is upstream's success-edge id for the implicit error transition, and `8` (`TRANSITION_DESTROY`) has no enumerator because `trigger_transition` rejects it. Pinned against the message constants by `packages/api/nros-cpp/tests/compile/lifecycle_transition_ids.cpp`. Why an enum exists at all: `trigger_transition(LifecycleTransition)` is the type-safe overload that makes a wrong-id call a compile error where the `uint8_t` overload made it a silent wrong transition -- issue 1099 was exactly that byte, in nano-ros's OWN numbering, crossing four of eight upstream ids. Same shape as `cpp:LifecycleState` (ours-only `enum class` where rclcpp has an object) and the same reason. OUR LANGUAGES now AGREE on the name: Rust `nros::LifecycleTransition` (`rust:LifecycleTransition`) and C `NROS_LIFECYCLE_TRANSITION_*` carry the same numbers.
